name: El Salvador
summary_text: El Salvador demands real caution from trans visitors — in an unusual transition. Historically it was among the world's most dangerous places for trans women (documented life expectancy of 35 years; the Camila Díaz Córdova case — a trans woman deported from the US and killed — became the first hate-crime homicide prosecution of its kind). Since 2022, President Bukele's gang crackdown collapsed the national homicide rate by ~98% (107 to 1.9 per 100k), dramatically reducing the gang violence that drove much anti-trans predation. The trade-off is a state of exception with mass arbitrary detention (75,000+ imprisoned, minimal due process) — a risk mechanism that falls on anyone police decide to target, including gender-nonconforming people, with no effective recourse. There is no legal gender recognition law (administrative name change only), no SOGI hate-crime statute, and no institutional protection infrastructure.

sources.title: Transgender Asylum-Seeker’s Death Could Prompt El Salvador’s First Hate Crime Homicide Conviction
sources.claim_summary: Foreign Policy (Mar 2020): 'Transgender Asylum-Seeker's Death Could Prompt El Salvador's First Hate Crime Homicide Conviction' — a landmark case on anti-trans violence in the justice system.

sources.title: The Decade-Long Evolution of Latin America's Homicide Rates
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This InSight Crime article is about Latin America's homicide rates generally, not El Salvador's LGBT situation specifically; included as general security context.

Academic article (Dilemas, 2024): 'Denied deaths: Profile of homicides against LGBTI+ people in El Salvador (2000-2020)' - builds a profile of crimes, victims and perpetrators of anti-LGBTI+ homicides in El Salvador over two decades.

sources.title: “Every Day I Live in Fear”: Violence and Discrimination Against LGBT People in El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, and Obstacles to Asylum in the United States | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report (Oct 2020) 'Every Day I Live in Fear': violence and discrimination against LGBT people in El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras, and obstacles to US asylum - opens with the story of Camila Díaz Córdova, a 29-year-old trans woman who fled El Salvador and was later killed there.

HRW report (Jan 2021) 'I'm Lucky to Still Be Alive': violence and discrimination against LGBT people in El Salvador - full report with recommendations to the president, attorney general, congress and ministries.

sources.title: El Salvador: Police Officers Convicted for Transgender Murder | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (July 2020): 'El Salvador: Police Officers Convicted in Transgender Murder' - three police officers convicted for the killing of Camila Díaz Córdova, a rare case of accountability for anti-trans violence.

sources.title: El Salvador lawmakers pass enhanced hate crime penalties
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Sept 2015): El Salvador lawmakers approved enhanced hate-crime penalties covering crimes motivated by the victim's sexual orientation or gender identity.
